Otaru is a municipality in Hokkaido Prefecture, in the Hokkaido region of Japan. Hokkaido is known for one prefecture covering a fifth of the country, from Hakodate in the south to Wakkanai on the Russian sea border.

What is an akiya in Otaru?

An akiya (空き家) is an abandoned or vacant house in Japan. Otaru has 404 akiya properties currently listed, ranging from traditional Japanese homes to more modern structures. These properties are often available at significantly lower prices than typical real estate.

Can foreigners buy property in Otaru?

Yes, foreigners can freely purchase property in Otaru and anywhere in Japan. There are no restrictions on foreign ownership of real estate in Japan. However, buying property does not grant residency rights. We recommend working with a licensed real estate agent familiar with Otaru.

How much do akiya cost in Otaru?

Akiya prices in Otaru vary widely depending on location, condition, and size. Some properties are available for under ¥1,000,000 (around $7,000 USD), while others in better condition or locations may cost more. Some may even be free but require renovation.

What should I know before buying an akiya in Otaru?

Before purchasing an akiya in Otaru, consider: (1) Property condition - many need renovation, (2) Location accessibility, (3) Legal requirements - clear title and no liens, (4) Ongoing costs - taxes, maintenance, utilities, (5) Language barriers - consider a bilingual agent.
